messages:
molly: Heads-up — noticed a bunch of customer tickets where clients see 503s for what we think are quota/backpressure events. Confusing for them and our runbooks.
kevin: Can you paste an example? 503 usually means downstream or infra failure; 429 is rate-limit.
jess: We historically used 503 for 'degraded routing' (soft-fail) when fallback model was unavailable. That collided with quota enforcement in a few routes.
molly: Exactly. One customer thought our service was down and retried aggressively, which worsened load.
anya: From product/console POV, we need deterministic client signals so customers can show clear UI. 503 vs 429 ambiguity breaks dashboard alerts + SLA contracts.
lee: Tech detail: some paths run through the routing proxy that returns 503 if no compatible replica; quota reagents live later in the stack and returned 429. So same surface behavior but different origins.
kevin: Proposed: standardize surface semantics. Use 429 for client-visible throttling/quota and 503 for platform-level failures only. For soft-degrades we should return 200 with a structured body + warning when possible.
jess: Returning 200 for degraded output might be risky for some SDKs (they assume success semantics). We need a clear contract + migration window.
molly: What about headers? If we keep status differences we can add explicit headers so clients can programmatically decide. e.g.
```
X-Redwood-Client-Quarantine: soft|hard
X-Redwood-Retryable: true|false
Retry-After: 30
```
kevin: I like headers. Also add a machine-readable subcode: `err_kind=quota_soft` / `err_kind=routing_no_replica` — helps telemetry and console grouping.
anya: Console side: we can map those header/subcodes to badges and tooltips. For soft-quota we show a 'degraded results' badge + link to cost/dashboard guidance. For hard-quota -> show 'quota reached' and link to upgrade path.
lee: Telemetry ask: ensure SPAN tags include origin (routing|quota|model) and subcode. Current dashboards aggregate 5xx vs 4xx only which hides the story.
jess: Rollout plan idea:
- Phase A: start emitting headers and `err_kind` while keeping current status codes (2 weeks)
- Phase B: SDKs add detection for headers and prefer header semantics (canary users) (4 weeks)
- Phase C: flip status codes to standardized mapping with a deprecation notice (8 weeks)
molly: Sounds sensible. Who owns phases?
kevin: Eng-platform owns header design + gateway changes (i'll take A).
lee: Eng-infra handles span tagging + dashboards (i'll take telemetry work for A/B).
anya: Product will own console badging + copy (I'll draft text).
jess: SDKs team will implement header parsing and a runtime toggle (I'll coordinate with them).
sre-bot: Note created: #INC-2026 - inconsistent-status-codes -> assigned to eng-platform, eng-infra, product, SDKs.
molly: Copy for console/help center (first pass):
- For 429: "Request rate exceeded. Reduce frequency or request a higher quota. See quota settings."
- For soft-degrade (header `err_kind=quota_soft`): "Results degraded due to load; try again or enable caching. We may fallback to a cheaper model."
- For 503: "Temporary platform issue. We are retrying; if persistent open a support ticket."
kevin: Slight tweak: include `Retry-After` where meaningful + include `err_id` for debugging (short id token).
anya: Can we make the console show a one-click 'why this happened' panel using the err_kind + err_id mapping?
lee: Yes, telemetry will populate a small event store keyed by err_id. We need retention rules but doable.
jess: Risk: some partners parse status codes strictly. We should publish a compatibility guide and a header-first migration strategy.
molly: Agreed. Action items: A) kevin add header proto + RFC in eng-platform docs by EOD Friday. B) lee wire a dashboard sample for err_kind by next Wed. C) anya draft console copy + tooltip variants by next Tue. D) jess sync SDKs and prepare canary.
kevin: I'll open the PR for header names and a tiny compatibility table. Using `X-Redwood-ErrKind` and `X-Redwood-ErrID` as canonical names.
anya: UI copy note: short messages in API responses + longer link in console to avoid noise.
molly: Thanks all. If no objections i'll start a short-cadence weekly sync for the rollout. :thumbsup:
kevin: +1
lee: +1
jess: +1
anya: +1
